text.p: The stock of Kent Electronics Corp. fell sharply Friday, a day after the company said it expected earnings to drop in the second quarter.
The stock was down $5.25 to $16.125 in afternoon trading and it was second biggest percentage loser on the the New York Stock Exchange with a 24 percent loss.
The Houston-based electronics manufacturer and distributor said on Thursday that it expected lower earnings per share of 24 cents to 25 cents for its fiscal second quarter ending Sept. 28.
In last year's second quarter, the company posted revenues of $90 million and net income of $6 million, or 29 cents a share.
The company said the figures reflected weakness in electronics manufacturing and distribution. It also said that it has cut senior management compensation and it is cutting staff to reduce costs.
The extent of the cuts in management compensation and employees was not immediately available. Kent said it was expecting revenues between $100 million and $106 million for its second quarter.
